AGENTIC STUDIO — INDUSTRIAL GROUND-STATE VISUALIZER

Detailed R&D, Architecture, Implementation, Compliance & Proof-of-Concept DocumentationReport #5 • Version 1.0 • August 2026

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-016-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Visualizer Detailed Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: Visualization | Section: 1. Executive Summary | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: AgentVisualizer, LangStudioUI, GraphRenderer]

The Agentic Studio Visualizer is the human-facing and machine-grounded representation of an industrial environment inside AI-ConneX. It should not be treated as a conventional dashboard. Its architectural role is to establish and render an Industrial Ground-State: a current, contextual representation of assets, machines, processes, telemetry, relationships, alerts, models, agents, knowledge and permitted tools.

The Visualizer receives the user's operational intent from Jane/Chatbot and consumes lineage and intelligence produced by Data Studio and ML Studio. It transforms these inputs into a live operational view that an industrialist can understand without interpreting datasets, ML metrics, database schemas or raw telemetry.

The Visualizer is not the agent's decision engine. The Agent Runtime can consume the same Ground-State through APIs. This separation prevents the UI from becoming the system of record.

Important pipeline clarification: the Visualizer is downstream of ML Studio, while Data Profiler is upstream in Data Studio. Therefore the Visualizer's normal output is NOT an input to Data Profiler. Its primary outputs go to Agent Builder, Agent Spec, Agent Runtime, monitoring and governance. A separate, versioned operational-feedback path can later create a NEW Data Studio profiling run.

AI-ConneX can expose domain-specific mathematical views when they help explain operational state. The calculation engine should remain separate from the renderer.

FFT/frequency spectrum for vibration or acoustic signals.

Time-domain trends and rolling statistics.

Spectrograms where appropriate.

Control-chart style monitoring.

Correlation/relationship views.

Energy/load curves.

Threshold bands and confidence intervals.

Residual/error plots.

A mathematical visualization must carry units, sampling assumptions, method and timestamp.

FFT_RESULT+-- result_uid+-- source_stream_uid+-- sampling_rate_hz+-- window_function+-- window_size+-- overlap+-- transform_version+-- generated_at+-- source_hash

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-016-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Visualizer Detailed Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: Visualization | Section: 15. R&D Problem Statement | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: AgentVisualizer, LangStudioUI, GraphRenderer]

Industrial environments are fragmented across ERP, MES, SCADA, PLC/IoT systems, databases, files and human procedures. A visual layer that merely charts streams does not solve the semantic problem. AI-ConneX therefore treats visualization as a projection of a structured Ground-State that unifies operational entities, relationships, live state, models and knowledge.

Research on manufacturing digital twins and knowledge graphs supports this direction. An IFAC case study at Atlas Copco Airpower describes a cognitive digital twin using an ontology-based knowledge graph to improve manufacturing-system analysis. More recent work also explores multi-layer knowledge graphs, digital twins and explainable/agentic maintenance systems.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-016-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Visualizer Detailed Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: Visualization | Section: 16. Key Failures and AI-ConneX Mitigations | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: AgentVisualizer, LangStudioUI, GraphRenderer]



| Failure | Risk | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dashboard-only design | No asset semantics | Ground-State + topology |
| Stale data shown as live | Wrong decisions | Freshness states + timestamps |
| Hallucinated asset | Unsafe context | Ground-State authority |
| Wrong asset association | Bad alerts | Stable asset IDs + lineage |
| Prediction detached from machine | No actionable context | Model → asset mapping |
| Alert overload | Users ignore alerts | Deduplication + severity + policy |
| Color-only communication | Poor interpretation | Evidence + numeric state |
| Visualizer becomes source of truth | State divergence | Canonical backend Ground-State |
| Agent executes through UI | Unsafe coupling | Tool gateway + authorization |
| Unsafe autonomy | Physical/operational risk | Human approval policies |
| Overloaded screen | User confusion | Role-based views |
| Math plot misunderstood | Wrong conclusions | Units + method metadata |
| Multi-site leakage | Privacy/security risk | RBAC/ABAC + tenant isolation |
| Conflicting sources | Incorrect state | Precedence + explicit conflict state |
| Frontend outage | Operational blindness | Independent APIs + graceful degradation |

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-016-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Visualizer Detailed Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: Visualization | Section: 31. Compliance Report #5 | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: AgentVisualizer, LangStudioUI, GraphRenderer]

This is an architectural compliance assessment, not a certification. Actual compliance depends on sector, country, safety classification, contracts and deployment conditions.

NIST AI RMF organizes AI risk management around Govern, Map, Measure and Manage and calls for documented human oversight and production monitoring. NIST's 2026 work on monitoring deployed AI systems further highlights the operational difficulty of maintaining monitoring at scale. These principles support the AI-ConneX design of continuous observability, provenance and explicit human oversight.

| Control | AI-ConneX control | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Governance | Ground-State ownership/versioning | Ground-State manifest |
| Traceability | Data/model/asset provenance | UIDs and lineage |
| Human oversight | Approval state | Agent/action audit |
| Transparency | Evidence/model metadata | Explainability view |
| Monitoring | Freshness/source health | Telemetry and health logs |
| Security | RBAC/ABAC/tenant isolation | Access logs |
| Integrity | Hashes/source provenance | Manifest hashes |
| Safety | No unrestricted browser control | Tool gateway + policy |
| Reproducibility | Versioned math parameters | Math metadata |
| Incident response | Timeline/audit events | Event store |
| Third-party risk | Pinned dependencies/SBOM | SBOM + scans |

H2: Asset/model/telemetry lineage improves perceived trust and explainability.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-016-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Visualizer Detailed Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: Visualization | Section: 37. Data Profiler Relationship — Correct Contract | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: AgentVisualizer, LangStudioUI, GraphRenderer]

The project template asks what the Visualizer outputs as an input for Data Profiler. In the architecture established so far, that is not the normal direction. Data Profiler is upstream; Agentic Studio is downstream.

PRIMARY FLOWData Profiler    |Data Studio    |ML Studio    |Agentic Studio Visualizer    |+---+-------------------+|                       |Agent Builder       Agent RuntimeNOT:Visualizer -> Data Profiler

A feedback loop is possible, but it is a NEW lineage branch:

Agentic Studio    |operational feedback    vFeedback Dataset    |Data Studio Compiler    |NEW Data Profiler Run    |NEW Manifest / Version

Feedback may include telemetry-derived datasets, alert outcomes, user overrides, incidents, maintenance outcomes and agent performance. It must never silently mutate the historical profile.

[Document: DOC-DOC-SPEC-016-V1 | Title: AI-ConneX Agentic Studio Visualizer Detailed Documentation | Studio: AgenticStudio | Category: Visualization | Section: 42. Final Takeaway | Authority: A]
[Governed Subsystems: AgentVisualizer, LangStudioUI, GraphRenderer]

The Visualizer should remain in AI-ConneX, but it should be defined as a Ground-State interface rather than a decorative dashboard. Data Studio makes industrial data usable; ML Studio makes predictive intelligence; Agentic Studio turns those assets into continuously observable and actionable industrial intelligence.

The strongest design rule is: the Ground-State is the canonical context; the Visualizer displays and explains it; Agent Runtime reasons and acts; the policy/tool layer authorizes actions; and Data Profiler remains upstream unless a deliberate operational-feedback loop creates a new Data Studio run.
